subject: crs
topic: Themes from the Epistles: Christian living, humility, civic duty, the second coming

kept.q: In Romans chapter 13, Paul teaches that Christians should submit to civil government. What reason does he give for this instruction?
options: Because the authorities are perfect and cannot make mistakes
Because governing authorities have been established by God
Because believers should only obey leaders they personally like
Because civil law is more important than God's law
kept.explanation: Paul says every soul should be subject to governing authorities because there is no authority except from God, and those that exist are appointed by Him. This teaches respect for lawful government as part of civic duty. See Romans 13:1-2.
kept.pidgin: Paul talk say every person must dey obey government because na God put authority for der place. Dis one na about civic duty wey Christian suppose show. Na Romans 13:1-2.

kept.q: In Philippians chapter 2, Paul uses the example of Jesus Christ who humbled Himself and took the form of a servant. What virtue is Paul teaching the Philippian believers through this example?
kept.explanation: Paul tells believers to have the same mind as Christ, who humbled Himself and became obedient even to death on the cross. This passage is a model of humility for Christian living. See Philippians 2:5-8.
kept.pidgin: Paul tell believers make dem get mind like Jesus, wey humble Imself go die for cross. Na humility im dey teach as example for Christian living. Na Philippians 2:5-8.

kept.q: In 1 Thessalonians 5:2, Paul describes how the day of the Lord will come upon unprepared people. What image does he use to describe its sudden and unexpected arrival?
options: A shepherd searching for a lost sheep
kept.explanation: Paul writes that the day of the Lord will come as a thief in the night, meaning it will arrive suddenly when people least expect it. This warns believers to stay watchful and ready for Christ's second coming. See 1 Thessalonians 5:2.
kept.pidgin: Paul talk say the day of the Lord go come like how thief dey enter night time, nobody go sabi when e go reach. E dey warn believers make dem ready for Christ second coming. Na 1 Thessalonians 5:2.

kept.q: In Romans 12:1, Paul appeals to believers to present their bodies to God in a particular way as an act of reasonable worship. What does he call this offering?
kept.explanation: Paul urges believers to present their bodies as a living sacrifice, holy and acceptable to God, which he calls their reasonable service. This teaches that true worship involves daily holy living, not just rituals. See Romans 12:1.
kept.pidgin: Paul beg believers make dem give dia body as living sacrifice wey holy and dey please God, e call am reasonable service. E mean say real worship na how person dey live holy everyday. Na Romans 12:1.

kept.q: James, in his epistle, teaches about the relationship between faith and works. According to James 2:17, what is faith that has no accompanying works described as?
kept.explanation: James teaches that faith without works is dead, meaning genuine faith must show itself through good deeds and righteous living. This is a key theme in the practical Christian living taught in his epistle. See James 2:17.
kept.pidgin: James talk say faith wey no get work na dead faith, e mean say correct faith must show through good deeds and righteous life. Na im be practical Christian living wey James dey teach. Na James 2:17.

kept.q: In 2 Peter 3:10, Peter describes the day of the Lord coming unexpectedly like a thief, after which the heavens shall pass away with a great noise. What does he say will happen to the elements on that day?
options: They will be rolled up like a scroll
They will melt with fervent heat
They will shine brighter than the sun
kept.explanation: Peter describes that on the day of the Lord, the heavens will pass away with a great noise, and the elements will melt with fervent heat, showing the dramatic and total transformation that will accompany Christ's second coming. See 2 Peter 3:10.
kept.pidgin: Peter talk say on the day of the Lord, heaven go pass away with loud noise and the elements go melt because of strong heat. Dis one dey show the kain serious change wey go happen when Christ come back. Na 2 Peter 3:10.

kept.q: In 1 Timothy 2:1-2, Paul instructs Timothy that prayers, intercessions, and thanksgiving should be made for kings and all in authority. What reason does Paul give for making such prayers?
options: So that the church can gain political power
So that believers may lead a peaceful and quiet life in godliness
So that kings will give money to the church
So that unbelievers will be punished by God
kept.explanation: Paul instructs that prayers be made for kings and all in authority so that believers may lead a quiet and peaceable life in all godliness and honesty. This shows that civic responsibility includes praying for leaders for the good of society. See 1 Timothy 2:1-2.
kept.pidgin: Paul talk say make dem dey pray for kings and leaders so dat believers go fit live quiet and peaceful life wey get godliness. Dis one show say civic duty include to dey pray for leaders for society good. Na 1 Timothy 2:1-2.

kept.q: According to Hebrews 13:17, believers are told to obey those who rule over them in the church because such leaders watch for their souls as those who must give what to God?
options: An account for the souls under their care
kept.explanation: Hebrews 13:17 teaches that church leaders watch over the souls of believers because they will give an account to God for how they led them. Believers are therefore urged to obey and submit to such leaders joyfully. See Hebrews 13:17.
kept.pidgin: Hebrews 13:17 teach say church leaders dey watch over believers soul because dem go give account to God for how dem lead dem. Na im make believers suppose dey obey dia leaders well well. Na Hebrews 13:17.
